text:
owen: quick idea — what if our gateway used live telemetry to steer model selection? e.g. alias health score, recent latency p50, and error rate feed into routing decisions. start small with a/b canary cohorts?

maya: curious. how do you compute alias health? rolling window? per-region?

owen: yes rolling 5m and 1h aggregates. per-region if region header present. health = (success_rate * 0.6) + (latency_score * 0.3) + (quota_margin * 0.1) — prototype only.

sasha: watch out for feedback loops — routing away from a model lowers its traffic and might mask degradations. we need minimum sampling to keep stats stable.

julian: agree. add forced sample of 1% traffic to each alias for cold stats. also keep a last-known-good fingerprint so we can revert routing if telemetry is noisy.

owen: good call. also thinking of compatibility buckets: tag model variants with compatibility bits (tokenizer_v2=true, kvcache_support=false). routing rules must respect required bits from route / header.

maya: example rule?

owen: `if header("x-model-compat") contains "tokenizer_v2" and alias.health>0.8 then route -> alias:stable_v2 else fallback -> alias:stable_compat`

infra-bot: NOTE: rollout bot will log any cross-alias fallback events to /observability/model-routing/fallbacks (severity: info).

devex: UI/console implication — we should surface an "alias health" sparkline on route pages and show why an alias was deprioritized (latency / errors / quota). otherwise product teams will be confused.

julian: +1 on explanation. also add a recent-sample histogram so you can tell if a spike is from one tenant.

maya: quota margin — does that mean remaining reserved tokens or commit headroom? tenants with tight reserved commits might need priority routing.

owen: right now prototype uses per-tenant reserved capacity fraction (1.0 - used_fraction). But maybe we need tiered overrides: enterprise tenants bypass health-based deprioritization up to their SLA.

sasha: implement override policies carefully: order of evaluation must be deterministic. proposal: 1) explicit tenant override 2) header constraints (compat flags) 3) telemetry health scoring 4) fallback policy. document in routing DSL.

devex: could we encode that as a small DSL snippet? something like:

```
route {
  match: path.startsWith("/v1/generate")
  require: [tokenizer_v2]
  priority: tenant_override > header > telemetry
  telemetry: {
    sampling: 0.01,
    windows: [300, 3600],
    actions: { if health<0.75 -> fallback(alias:compat) }
  }
}
```

julian: I like it. needs exact semantics for `health` and how we compute `latency_score` (normalize to 0..1). also ensure disabled models don't appear in alias list for routing.

maya: how do we prevent thrash when health oscillates around threshold? hysteresis? a minimum dwell time?

owen: yes, add hysteresis & cooldown: once an alias is demoted, it must meet a higher threshold (0.85) for 2 consecutive windows to be promoted. cooldown 10m.

infra-bot: FYI: current routing engine supports TTL-based pinning and header-driven overrides but not metric-driven scoring. will need infra changes and migration plan.

devex: UX question — when a model is fallbacked for a tenant, do we surface that event to the tenant logs (so they know their model got routed)?

sasha: should be opt-in — privacy and noise considerations. maybe only for tenants with debug flag or internal ones.

julian: action items: 1) owen + infra to sketch metrics (health formula, windows) 2) sasha to prototype sampling + hysteresis 3) devex to mock console health widgets 4) maya to list required compatibility bits for product teams.

owen: I'll start a small experiment on dev cluster routing 1% traffic for 24h. will post results. :rocket: 

devex: please add telemetry events to the routing events stream with fields: `chosen_alias`, `fallback_reason`, `health_score`, `tenant_id` (pseudonymized for public dashboards).

maya: one more thought — make fallback reason granular: latency_spike vs tokenization_error vs quota_exhausted. helps debugging.

owen: noted. thanks all — will update after experiment. :thumbsup:
